steps.label: Set the period equal to 2/3
steps.margin_note: First mark. Same as the cosine version — sine has the same period formula, so nothing changes but the name.
lines: Let sin kx be the required sine function.

recall.must_convey: That sin kx is assumed and 2π/k set equal to 2/3.
accept: let it be sin k x and set two pi over k equal to two thirds
equate the period formula to two by three
sine has the same period formula as cosine
sin k x anukoni two pi by k equals two by three
set up the equation for k

steps.why: sin and cos have identical periods — only tan differs. So the same formula serves both.
common_mistakes: Using π/k because it is a sine.

steps.label: Solve for k and write the function
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Cross-multiplying gives 2k = 6π, so k = 3π.

lines.text: ∴ sin(3πx) is the required sine function

recall.must_convey: That k = 3π, so the function is sin(3πx).
accept: cross multiplying gives two k equals six pi so k is three pi and the function is sin three pi x
k is three pi so the answer is sin of three pi x
the required function is sin three pi x
k equals three pi, function sin three pi x
solve to get three pi and write the sine function

steps.why: A period smaller than 2π needs a coefficient larger than 1 — and 3π is indeed larger, which checks out.
common_mistakes: Getting k = π/3 by dividing the wrong way.
